document.title: feat(host-control): let Deck Apps call linked computers through built-in and custom plugins
document.summary: Deck Apps call typed commands on linked computers through a new SDK client, companion CLI and always-on LAN Listener; custom plugins ship as packages and push events.

sources.author: chatgpt-codex-connector
sources.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject unauthorized peers before reading their bodies**

When a non-linked LAN peer sends a slow or concurrent request, `reply` waits for `readBody` to finish before checking `isAllowed`; `readBody` continues consuming the stream and buffers up to 64 KiB per request, so denied peers can tie up sockets and memory before receiving a 403. Check the peer before reading the body, or abort unauthorized requests immediately, so the allowlist also protects availability.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

sources.label: cursor on PR #144
sources.author: cursor
sources.body: Risk: high. This adds a boot-time LAN HTTP listener, persisted host links, plugin loading, and long-polling host events, so it is above the medium approval threshold and was not approved. Cursor Bugbot was skipped and no Security Agent check ran; human review is needed and no reviewers were assigned.

lookFor: [#111](source:s4) asks for a separate link listener on 8798 that runs only while the Host Control screen is open. `lan_listener.c` serves `/link` and `/upload` together from boot instead; [PR #144](source:s1) says the first setup felt clunky.

[#111](source:s4) names `nativeGetHostControlUrl` and one link in `host-control-link.json`. At head `nativeGetHostControlLinks` returns an array from `host-control-links.json`, and the payload gains `id`; [PR #144](source:s1) lists this deviation.

[#109](source:s2) keeps command definitions internal because VitaDeck owns the companion, and offers a default `host`. At head `defineHostPlugin` is public and `createHostClient` takes a plugin; [PR #144](source:s1) lists plugins as a deviation.

[#110](source:s3) allows no computer-acting commands before the credential decision, and gates later ones behind `enable`. At head a custom plugin command runs any code, and `server.ts` consults no `enable` list. No source says why custom plugins are exempt.
[PR #144](source:s1) says only read-only built-ins exist. `core.notify` is a built-in that `server.ts` runs for any allowed peer, and its notice reaches every Deck App watching `core`.

[#110](source:s3) runs the companion from source with `tsx` and saves one `vita`. At head it is a rolldown bundle with a `vitadeck-host-companion` bin, and `cli.ts` reads `vitas`. The deviation list in [PR #144](source:s1) names neither.

[PR #144](source:s1) says the LAN Listener uses port 8787. `lan_listener_start` tries 8787 through 8796, and `link` assumes 8787 when the address names no port, so a Vita that fell forward needs the port the Shell shows.

[Cursor's review](source:s7) says human review is needed, no reviewers were assigned, and Bugbot and the security check did not run. The review table in [PR #144](source:s1) lists only Claude, Grok and Muse, and no source shows a human review.

groups.why: [PR #145](source:s5) says a custom plugin used to mean an npm package of its own.
groups.summary: `build` writes a Deck App, a `.vdplugin` package and their zips, or only the plugin when `entry` is absent. A plugin-only `dev` rejects a URL and uploads nothing.

attention.note: `build` runs the Deck App and plugin builds in one call, and `buildDeckApp` deletes the old `.vdapp.zip` first. When the plugin fails, `build` throws before any archive is written, so `dev` uploads nothing that cycle and `dist` has no `.vdapp.zip`, while the last good `.vdplugin` survives. Decide whether one failure should block both.

groups.title: Plugin install and reload
groups.why: [PR #145](source:s5) says a globally installed companion could not load a plugin installed somewhere else.
groups.summary: `install` stages and loads a package before renaming it into the plugins folder, and `start` reloads plugins when watched folders change.

attention.note: `install` calls `loadHostPluginPackage` on the staged package, so its code runs with the user's permissions before any command and before the built-in id check. Once loaded, `server.ts` lets any Deck App on a linked Vita call any plugin, because the peer check knows only the IP. Decide whether that is enough before credentials exist.

notes.body: One package that fails to load stops `start`; the ledger declined skipping it.

groups.title: Events by long-polling
groups.summary: `core.events` holds a request until the plugin's next event, and `watchHostEvents` keeps one wait open, passing `next` as `after`.

attention.note: `watchHostEvents` keeps one native fetch open per watch, and `fetch.c` runs each fetch on its own thread. A computer that stops answering costs 29 s to time out and 30 s more to retry. [PR #144](source:s1) rejects WebSocket and SSE in ADR 0004. Decide whether a held thread per watch suits the Vita.

questions: Why does `watchHostEvents` keep its `after` cursor when the resolved host changes?

fileNotes.js/packages/host-companion/src/events.ts: New `createEventLog`; the PR says 100 events per plugin.
Adds `watchHostEvents` with a 29 s wait and 5 s or 30 s retry.
fileNotes.js/packages/host-companion/test/server.t: `alertsWithEmit` checks that a held wait answers on emit.
fileNotes.js/packages/sdk/test/host-control.test.t: The PR names `next` as `after` and a callback stopping the watch.

groups.title: Fetch cancels on Deck App stop
groups.summary: `fetch_shutdown` marks every pending fetch cancelled and `fetch_progress_cb` aborts it, so a held wait no longer delays a stop.

attention.note: `fetch_shutdown` cancels every pending fetch, not only event waits. A Deck App that posts a save and then stops used to block the stop until the request ended; at head the transfer aborts at curl's next progress call, about a second later, and the save may not arrive. Decide whether all fetches should share this.

notes.body: A nonzero return makes curl abort the transfer.

commits.subject: fix(host-companion): relink attempts run one at a time and re-read the config
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Retries for different Vitas ran on independent timers, and each save
wrote the same temporary file from a config read before the request.
All attempts now share one queue, a failure is logged, and linkVita
reads the config again just before changing its Vitas. Also list
unknown_link with the other link endpoint codes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat(host-control): the companion relinks its Vitas on every start
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
A new computer IP or companion port broke commands until the user ran
`link` again. `start` now re-sends the link to every Vita in its config
with `relink: true`, which VitaDeck applies only to a link it still has,
so a computer forgotten in the Shell is not linked back: VitaDeck
answers 404 `unknown_link` and the companion drops that Vita. A Vita
that does not answer is retried every 30 s. The host-control demo asks
for capabilities again when a relink changes the URL.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat(shell): one LAN Listener for upload and link, on from startup
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Setting up a Deck App with a Host Control Plugin needed two Shell steps
and two addresses: start Upload for `vitadeck dev`, then open Host
Control for `link`. The upload server now also serves `POST /link`,
VitaDeck starts it at boot, and the Shell row turns it off and on. Both
CLIs take the same Vita address (port 8787).

commits.subject: fix(host-companion): start plugin lifecycles after binding the port
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
A busy port no longer leaves a plugin's timers running. Stopping twice is a
no-op, each plugin keeps its own 100 events, and core.events answers
unknown_plugin for a plugin the companion has not loaded. The SDK says a
throw from a watch callback stops watching.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat(host-control): computers push events to Deck Apps by long-polling
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
A plugin declares Host Control Events next to its commands and emits them
from a start(emit) lifecycle the companion runs while it is loaded. The
companion numbers recent events, and core.events holds a request until the
plugin's next event or 25 s. watchHostEvents in the SDK keeps one such
request open, so an event reaches the Vita within one round trip. core.notify
and `vitadeck-host-companion notify` let any script send a notice, which the
host-control demo shows.

Stopping a Deck App now cancels its pending fetches through curl's progress
callback, so a held request no longer stalls a reload or shutdown.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: docs(skills): add vitadeck-host-control and cover Host Control in the others
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
The new public skill covers running and linking the Host Companion, calling
plugins from a Deck App, writing plugins with a Deck App or standalone, the

commits.subject: feat(host-control): a Deck App's plugin ships as a .vdplugin package and zip
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Plugins will carry more than code (scripts, data, binaries), so the single
bundled file becomes a package like the Deck App's: `vitadeck build` writes a
<slug>.vdplugin folder (manifest.json, companion.mjs, optional files/) and a
<slug>.vdplugin.zip. `hostPlugin` becomes { entry, files? }. The companion
installs archives or folders into ~/.vitadeck/plugins/<id>.vdplugin, loads the
entry by file URL so it finds its files through import.meta.url, and watches
package folders recursively.

commits.subject: feat(host-control): built-in plugins, .vdplugin files, vitadeck-host-companion
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
A Deck App now keeps its own Host Control Plugin in its project: `hostPlugin`
in vitadeck.config.json makes `vitadeck build` bundle the implementation into
one self-contained <slug>.vdplugin, and `vitadeck create --host-plugin`
scaffolds it. Users install that file with `vitadeck-host-companion install`;
the companion reloads installed and --plugin files when they change.

systemStats moves into the companion as a built-in, with its registry in
@vitadeck/sdk/host-control next to implementHostPlugin and HostCommandError.
The companion is a dependency-free bundled package with the
vitadeck-host-companion bin, and js/host-plugins is gone.
